raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old male with multiple myeloma on his eighth cycle of chemotherapy with bortezomib, lenalidomide (recently decreased to 10 mg po daily from 25 mg po daily), and dexamethasone presented with a two-week history of worsening blurriness and floaters in his right eye. An outside provider noted panuveitis and retinal whitening on examination. Anterior chamber paracentesis was negative for CMV, HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, and Toxoplasmosis. Oral valacyclovir and topical steroids and cycloplegics were started for presumed acute retinal necrosis, and the patient was referred to our institution for further diagnostic work-up and management. Of note, recent serum laboratory values revealed a normal white blood cell count (9.41 k/microL; range 4.5-11 k/microL) and neutrophilic profile (71.0%; range 39-69%) with negative CMV antigen and aerobic blood culture; lambda light chain immunoglobulins were significantly elevated (67.29 mg/L, range 5.7-26.3 mg/L) and alpha-2 globulin proteins were abnormally high on serum electrophoresis (0.93 g/dL, range 0.58-0.84 g/dL) as expected given his disease.
Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/60 in the right eye, 20/20 in the left. Pupils and intraocular pressures were normal. Slit lamp examination of the right eye revealed mild anterior chamber flare without cell, mild cataract, and 3+ cell in the anterior vitreous. Dilated funduscopic examination revealed vitreous haze, diffuse vascular sheathing, and a poorly-defined area of inferotemporal retinal whitening without associated hemorrhage (Figure 1). The left eye was normal. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography of the right eye showed no significant abnormalities aside from overlying hyperreflective vitreous debris (Figure 2). Fluorescein angiography demonstrated irregular vascular filling and blockage from vitreous debris (Figure 3).
Given the previous negative anterior chamber tap, worsening clinical exam, and high suspicion for infectious retinitis, the decision was made to proceed with a diagnostic vitrectomy. Diluted and undiluted vitreous biopsy were obtained via a 23-gauge pars plana vitrectomy. Intraoperatively, extensive retinal whitening and granular necrosis were observed along with diffuse vascular sheathing and perivascular inflammatory aggregates (Figure 4). Endolaser was placed 360 degrees prophylactically. The vitreous biopsy was sent for gram stain, cytology (to rule out malignant infiltration), fungal culture, Toxoplasmosis, AFB, VZV, EBV, CMV, HSV-1, HSV-2, and RPR testing.
On postoperative day 2, the vitreous PCR returned positive for CMV; all other tests were negative. The patient was switched from oral valacyclovir to valganciclovir 900 mg po twice daily. By postoperative day 3, the patient's visual acuity declined to 20/200 and there was an increase in anterior chamber cell. Hence, intravitreal foscarnet (2.4 mg/0.1 cc) was injected. At the postoperative week 1 visit, visual acuity had not improved, but the area of retinitis appeared less active (Figure 5). Repeat intravitreal foscarnet was given. Improvement continued over the first month with complete resolution of the patient's uveitis, vasculitis, and retinitis. By postoperative month 2, BCVA had improved to 20/63 without evidence of active disease. Five months after the vitreous biopsy, the patient remained without signs of intraocular infection with BCVA 20/50, mostly limited by cataract. Following cataract extraction one year later, his visual acuity was 20/25 with stable fundus findings (Figure 6).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old male with multiple myeloma presented with a 2-week history of worsening blurred vision and floaters in his right eye.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Receiving his eighth cycle of bortezomib, lenalidomide (recently reduced from 25 mg to 10 mg PO daily), and dexamethasone for lambda light-chain multiple myeloma, the patient developed 2 weeks of progressive right-eye blurriness and floaters. An outside ophthalmologist noted right panuveitis and retinal whitening, found a negative anterior chamber paracentesis PCR panel (negative for CMV, HSV-1/2, VZV, and Toxoplasma), started oral valacyclovir, topical steroids, and cycloplegics for presumed acute retinal necrosis, and referred him to our institution.
subjective.past_medical_history: Lambda light-chain multiple myeloma on cycle 8 of bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone chemotherapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 2 weeks of worsening right-eye blurred vision and floaters. Home medications: bortezomib, lenalidomide 10 mg daily, dexamethasone, oral valacyclovir, topical corticosteroids, and topical cycloplegics.

objective.physical_examination: Ophthalmic exam: best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) 20/60 OD (declining transiently to 20/200 on post-vitrectomy day 3 before recovering to 20/63 at month 2, 20/50 at month 5, and 20/25 after cataract extraction at 1 year) and 20/20 OS; normal pupils and IOPs OU; left eye normal. Right eye slit-lamp exam showed mild anterior chamber flare without cells, mild cataract, and 3+ anterior vitreous cells; dilated fundoscopy OD revealed vitreous haze, diffuse retinal vascular sheathing, and a poorly defined inferotemporal area of retinal whitening without retinal hemorrhage.
objective.routine_investigations: Recent labs: WBC 9.41 K/uL (ref 4.5-11 K/uL), neutrophils 71.0% (ref 39-69%), negative serum CMV antigenemia, negative aerobic blood cultures, elevated serum free lambda light chains (67.29 mg/L, ref 5.7-26.3 mg/L), and elevated alpha-2 globulins on SPEP (0.93 g/dL, ref 0.58-0.84 g/dL).
objective.advanced_workup: Outside anterior chamber aqueous paracentesis was negative for CMV, HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, and Toxoplasma. Right-eye spectral-domain OCT showed hyperreflective overlying vitreous debris; fluorescein angiography showed irregular retinal vascular filling and blockage from vitreous debris. Diagnostic 23-gauge pars plana vitrectomy (with prophylactic 360-degree endolaser retinopexy) demonstrated extensive intraoperative granular retinal whitening/necrosis, diffuse vascular sheathing, and perivascular inflammatory aggregates; vitreous biopsy PCR returned positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) on postoperative day 2 and negative for HSV-1/2, VZV, EBV, Toxoplasma, AFB, fungal/bacterial cultures, RPR, and malignant cytology.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of unilateral right-eye cytomegalovirus (CMV) panuveitis and necrotizing retinitis in a non-neutropenic multiple myeloma patient on bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone, confirmed by diagnostic 23-gauge pars plana vitrectomy fluid CMV PCR positivity despite a prior false-negative anterior chamber paracentesis and negative serum CMV antigenemia. Switched from oral valacyclovir to oral valganciclovir (900 mg twice daily) and treated with two weekly intravitreal foscarnet injections (2.4 mg/0.1 mL), achieving complete resolution of uveitis, retinal vasculitis, and retinitis within 1 month and final BCVA of 20/25 following cataract extraction 1 year later.
